answer.headline: ILM, HVN, SBN, PGD and PVU lead small-hub passenger CAGR from 2024 to 2025, with pooled NPIAS need of {F317} per CY2025 enplanement.

claims.text: ILM calculated enplaned-passenger CAGR, calendar 2025 versus calendar 2024, is {F147}.
HVN calculated enplaned-passenger CAGR, calendar 2025 versus calendar 2024, is {F143}.
SBN calculated enplaned-passenger CAGR, calendar 2025 versus calendar 2024, is {F215}.
PGD calculated enplaned-passenger CAGR, calendar 2025 versus calendar 2024, is {F189}.
PVU calculated enplaned-passenger CAGR, calendar 2025 versus calendar 2024, is {F201}.
ATW is the next airport in the same small-hub ranking, at {F83}, below PVU at {F201}, so the cutoff is not a tie.
For the selected airports together, estimated NPIAS development need per CY2025 enplanement is {F317}, from estimated NPIAS need {F318} and observed ACAIS enplanements {F319}.
Airport-level estimated need per CY2025 enplanement is ILM {F321}, HVN {F320}, SBN {F324}, PGD {F322} and PVU {F323}.
Estimated NPIAS development need is ILM {F326}, HVN {F325}, SBN {F329}, PGD {F327} and PVU {F328}.
The group figure {F317} follows {F317.definition} and uses the summed inputs {F318} and {F319}. It is the catalog aggregate for the set, not a screening score and not a valuation.

Nothing in these series identifies why passenger growth was faster at the selected airports, whether the development need will be funded, or whether the airports face unmet demand, tight terminal capacity, or strong returns. Those questions are outside this dataset.

assumptions: Small hub means FAA hub class S, the latest stored ACAIS hub class, held fixed across calendar 2024 and calendar 2025 rather than recomputed inside each year.

Fastest-growing means the highest calculated enplaned-passenger CAGR in that small-hub set. The window is full calendar 2025 versus full calendar 2024, as in {F147.period} for ILM, and the same window applies to HVN, SBN, PGD and PVU.

The pooled per-enplanement figure is the catalog aggregate over ILM, HVN, SBN, PGD and PVU with no airport split, so need and enplanements are summed before division. The enplanement window is CY2025. NPIAS need is the static 2025-2029 estimate.
limitations: T-100 passengers are segment enplanements, so a connecting passenger counts at each departure. The NPIAS ratio uses ACAIS calendar-year boardings. Growth and the per-enplanement denominator are different series.
NPIAS values are sponsor-reported AIP-eligible need estimates, not grants awarded and not a valuation. Unmet demand, terminal capacity, fares and profitability are not measured.
Airports without positive passenger totals in either calendar year would drop out of the CAGR ranking. No small-hub airport was unscored in this run.
This is a growth ranking plus a need ratio. It is not the investment screening model and it is not a recommendation to fund these airports.
